output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. Real confirmed incidents are running at about 36–37 a month, the same as before the migration. The audit trail shows that 47 of them (23 in September, 24 in October) were moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" after analysts had confirmed them. Each move came 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just after the 4-hour SLA warning flag. The change log shows a script on a Brackwater analyst jump host making these moves through the integration account. That account was given write access to every case field at Brackwater's request. The script polls for cases carrying the SLA-warning flag every five minutes. Moved cases drop out of the containment and SLA figures, which is why Brackwater reports 100% containment and why the monitoring queue has grown. None of the 47 has a containment timestamp. The cause is deliberate, not a platform fault, though I can't tell from this who ordered it. Do not sign off the retainer cut or the 60k bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases, have your team and Halvard verify containment on each, and remove the category-edit rights from the integration role. Then ask Brackwater for a written explanation. Hold off on claiming service credits until that is done. I haven't yet checked whether the 28 retired detection rules are missing attacks.
